muscle_guide_activation_svg_title: Motor neuron, neuromuscular junction, and muscle-fiber calcium release
muscle_guide_activation_svg_description: A cellular schematic identifies the motor axon, axon terminal, synaptic vesicles, synaptic cleft, nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, sarcolemma, T-tubule, and sarcoplasmic reticulum. Signal and ion highlights follow the selected step.
muscle_guide_sarcomere_svg_title: Actin, myosin, and Z discs during sarcomere shortening
muscle_guide_sarcomere_svg_description: A larger view identifies actin, myosin, and both Z discs. In the contraction step, Z discs move closer while actin filaments keep their length.
muscle_guide_focus_terminal: Motor axon · Axon terminal · Calcium channels
muscle_guide_focus_end_plate: Acetylcholine · Nicotinic receptors · Motor end plate
muscle_guide_terminal_detail: A motor-neuron action potential reaches the axon terminal and opens voltage-gated calcium channels. Calcium entry triggers synaptic vesicles to fuse with the membrane.
muscle_guide_end_plate_detail: Acetylcholine crosses the synaptic cleft and binds nicotinic receptors on the motor end plate. Sodium entry produces an end-plate potential that initiates a muscle action potential.
muscle_guide_calcium_detail: The action potential travels along the sarcolemma and down T-tubules. Voltage sensors activate ryanodine receptors in the sarcoplasmic reticulum, releasing calcium that binds troponin.
muscle_guide_sarcomere_detail: Calcium moves tropomyosin away from actin binding sites. ATP-powered myosin cross-bridge cycles pull thin filaments toward the sarcomere center; calcium reuptake and acetylcholine breakdown allow relaxation.
muscle_guide_clinical_change: Fewer functional nicotinic acetylcholine receptors reduce the motor end plate safety factor.
muscle_guide_clinical_effect: Repeated nerve signals are less likely to trigger reliable muscle-fiber action potentials.
muscle_guide_clinical_note: Educational comparison only — not a diagnostic view.
